observation_summary: The methods removeRangeMarker and removeDomainMarker in CategoryPlot and XYPlot throw a NullPointerException when called on a plot that has no markers initialized for the specified index.
hypothesis: The code attempts to retrieve an ArrayList of markers from a Map (foreground/background markers) using an index. If no markers have been added for that index, the Map returns null. The code then calls .remove(marker) on this null reference, causing a NullPointerException.
prediction: The code will require a null check on the 'markers' variable before calling .remove(marker). If 'markers' is null, the method should return false (indicating nothing was removed) instead of proceeding to the removal operation.
experiment_rationale: The stack trace points directly to the line where .remove() is called on the 'markers' object. Since the test case initializes a new plot (which has no markers), the map lookup for the index will return null, confirming the hypothesis that the missing null check is the root cause.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic missing guard (null check) for a collection that may not have been initialized. This fits the 'Checking' ODC type perfectly as it involves validating data (the result of the map lookup) before performing an operation that assumes the data exists.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The logic for removing a marker is correct; the issue is simply the lack of a guard against an uninitialized collection.
